title: Kashmir walnut harvest: how to plan your bulk order
excerpt: When Kashmir walnuts come in, how to choose between in-shell and kernels, what kernel colour tells you, and when to start talking to a supplier.
tldr: Kashmir walnuts are harvested around September and October, then need drying and sorting. Start planning before the harvest, decide between in-shell and kernels early, and agree the grade, moisture and crop year in writing.
keyTakeaways: Harvest runs around September and October, but timing shifts with weather and altitude.
In-shell nuts keep longer; kernels are ready to use but need more care.
In-shell nuts are graded by size, kernels by colour and by halves or pieces.
Always ask which crop year you're buying, especially late in the season.
content:
Walnuts are a once-a-year crop. If your production or resale depends on them, the harvest calendar sets your buying calendar. Here is how the Kashmir season works and what to decide at each stage.

When the harvest happens

Kashmir walnuts are generally harvested around September and October. The exact timing depends on the weather that year and on orchard altitude, so treat any date as an estimate until the crop is in.

Harvest isn't the same as availability. After the nuts come down, they have to be hulled, dried and sorted. Kernels take longer again, because the nuts must also be cracked and graded.

How to plan your order through the year

When

What to do

Before harvest

Share your likely volume, form and grade with suppliers, and ask how the crop is looking.

During harvest

Stay in touch. Expect estimates rather than firm details until nuts are dried and sorted.

After sorting

Ask for samples of the new crop, confirm grades and agree dispatch.

Later in the year

Check storage conditions and crop year carefully, especially for kernels.

In-shell or kernels?

This choice affects your costs, your storage and how long you can hold stock.

In-shell walnuts

The shell protects the nut, so in-shell walnuts generally keep longer and are easier to store. They suit retail packs and buyers with their own cracking capacity. Shell type matters as well: thin-shelled nuts are easier to crack by hand, while harder shells take more work.

Walnut kernels

Kernels are ready for food production and packing, with no cracking and less waste to deal with. However, walnuts are rich in oil, and once out of the shell they're more exposed to air, heat and light, which can turn them rancid. Vacuum packing and cool storage help a lot.

What the grades tell you

  • In-shell: usually graded by nut size. Agree the size range and how much variation is acceptable.

  • Kernels: usually graded by colour, such as extra light, light and light amber, and by form, such as halves or quarters. Lighter kernels with more intact halves generally cost more.

Pay for the grade your product needs. A bakery chopping kernels into a mix may not need whole light halves, while a retail pack where the kernels are on show might.

What to check on a sample

  • Taste and smell: a sharp, bitter or paint-like note suggests rancidity.

  • Kernels: look for even colour, and check for shrivelled pieces or mould.

  • Shells: crack a handful of in-shell nuts, because a good-looking shell can hide a poor kernel.

  • Moisture: ask for the figure. Too much moisture raises the risk of mould in storage.

What to agree in writing

  • Crop year, form and grade

  • Moisture limit

  • Packing type and pack size

  • Dispatch schedule, especially if you want the order split across several deliveries

  • What happens if the delivery doesn't match the approved sample

faqs.question: When are Kashmir walnuts harvested?
faqs.answer: Generally around September and October. Timing varies with the weather and orchard altitude, and the nuts still need hulling, drying and sorting after that.

faqs.question: Should I buy in-shell walnuts or kernels?
faqs.answer: In-shell walnuts generally keep longer and suit retail packs or buyers who can crack them. Kernels are ready to use but need more careful packing and storage.

faqs.question: How are walnut kernels graded?
faqs.answer: Usually by colour, such as extra light, light and light amber, and by form, such as halves or quarters.

faqs.question: How can I tell if walnut kernels have gone rancid?
faqs.answer: Taste and smell a sample. A sharp, bitter or paint-like note is the usual sign. Heat, air and light all speed this up.
